title: Лабиринты зрачков
text: Every glance quietly hides as Eternity in the labyrinths of your pupils.

title: Лабиринты зрачков
text: Tender hands untouched by fatigue, daily scars not yet stitched into warm cheeks.

title: Лабиринты зрачков
text: Eternity will pass before you say: "Forgive me..." Roses will wither. Orchids will shed their petals.

title: Лабиринты зрачков
text: One day pearl stems will wrap around you whole. Like rings on fingers – nectars of their sweet resin. You'll feel Eternity. She'll touch your lips, grow warmer, and your word will forget belonging. Something will happen, spill like ocean over granite's endless shore. Something will happen. June will draw you with its scorching sting.

title: Лабиринты зрачков
text: Frozen days... Eternity – she tempts.

title: Февральская катастрофа
text: February had already begun. Each day of this February was questioningly bleak and full of irritated egoism. Spring was already creeping across the sky in a light-blue silk "Triumph" slip with the finest lace of clouds.

title: Февральская катастрофа
text: She could only guess at the approaching catastrophe, Her Catastrophe. She waited for the irreversibly coming destruction, destruction to the foundation and beyond, destruction uncompromising and not subject to appeal, like a death sentence.

title: Февральская катастрофа
text: The ice-crusted snow, long covered with filth on the pavements, evoked nothing but disgust, only adding some sickly wariness to her step, slowing her path into yet another weekday nowhere.

title: Февральская катастрофа
text: The biting wind pierced her face, billowing her blue-black curls barely covered by a scarf.

title: Февральская катастрофа
text: Her premonitions were of an absurd, incoherent, but therefore intensely vivid nature, like the hallucinations of a patient floating above a couch that had long ago caved in the floor under the weight of illness.

title: Февральская катастрофа
text: The thaw at the end of January had behaved deceitfully, as usual.

title: Февральская катастрофа
text: This was how she met February. This was how Van Gogh once met his youth in London.

title: Французский снег
text: I swear to you by God, in whom I believe!.. This phrase, bursting wildly into morning from her muddled dream, was immediately scribbled in her notebook and thus thrown into the stream of daily recorded thoughts, plans, random quotes, desired and completed purchases and other paraphernalia without which Kira wouldn't stay afloat.

title: Французский снег
text: With this very paraphernalia, generously soaked in the aroma of strong coffee, she distracted herself from the monstrous depths where she'd dwelt as a sensitive and powerful fish all her 34 years. Otherwise it became terrifying—this constant search for something else, what seemed to her the true meaning in everything happening to her, in her, around her.

title: Французский снег
text: She dreamed of French snow and a sprawling fir by a chalet full of unknown boys and girls. "All have turned away. Together they have become worthless. There is no one who does good. Not even one. There is no one who understands, no one who seeks God. Their mouths are full of bitterness and cursing." Where did these words come from, ringing in her head?

title: Французский снег
text: She felt her breath becoming stifled, and again remembered Van Gogh's words: "What am I searching for? I'm at a dead end, in a kind of trap. What's my way out?" Vincent's field in Arles, flooded with scorching despair... "When will someone come and sit by your fire, and who knows, perhaps stay with you?"

title: Французский снег
text: "You took it all, didn't you? You took everything, I know." – said one of the garishly painted chicks in heavy luxury. "Finally you've come, darling" – she said, invitingly filling a martini glass. "Meet our Velena Adam. Welcome, sweetie. Let's fucking rock it tonight!!!"

title: Французский снег
text: The dead sleep of idleness. Youth with grimaces of luxury on its face and only some elegance of manner.

title: Французский снег
text: "I didn't take anything. I swear by God, in whom I believe!" – she answered, understanding that something terrible was beginning to happen, something wild in this forgotten world of her sick fantasies. Something rebellious suddenly stirred her soul, weakened here.

title: Французский снег
text: "You think you know a lot. But you know still too little. But I'll go with you and show you everything, you're here now – Everythiiiiing........" – hissed that chick with the sensually slipped strap on her cocktail dress.

title: Французский снег
text: She broke out into the air, threw herself into a sea of blinding snow. The lead of fir branches...

title: Французский снег
text: Dreams flogged with switches.

title: Французский снег
text: Her feet felt the strength flowing with blood and readiness to run, run headlong from this stale hell.

title: Французский снег
text: She had to wake up. Kira had to wake up.

title: Lagonie du romantisme
text: Kira Velerevich (known as Vel) was one of the best personal assistants to the seriously loaded and their families, those who could afford the most sought-after PAs. Plus Kira was special: she could write and loved it. In her diary, chalk on asphalt, in the margins of her bosses' daily schedules, and for glossy mags she wrote with pure pleasure. And in this too she became quite in demand. Today Vel was hammering out the lyrical finale of another "L'agonie du romantisme" column for Vehicle V. magazine, dedicated to Versace's new spring collection.

title: Lagonie du romantisme
text: "The sky keeps shifting from dull-sunny, slightly foggy to a clean bright blue that's vulgar in its intensity. A sky unpunctured by a single cloud reflects the crushed snow stained by first warmth. Raw windy March... Here the sun stops you, suddenly spilling shamelessly across your face and palms. Mood like an out-of-tune clarinet. Eyes squinting against sun try to hide all reality's absurdity, and entering a room simply flooded with light, you can't see things. Omnipresent dust mixed with its white March gold instantly scatters everywhere, and all of it: coals of February burnt out a week ago, heat of blood rushing to the heart - illuminates your melting life, like printing photographs, displaying them as memories in the showcase of a photo album. Laziness, having lain with you all winter under the blanket, apologizes for overstaying, and leaving, actually leaves. But She knows how to stand her ground. Sunny spring can be more caustic with us than any season. That's because She arrives sometimes completely unexpectedly and forces us to shed the dirty scales from our hearts, like scooping a full handful of change from a pocket. Spring and 'Clementie's' make us feel naked."

title: Lagonie du romantisme
text: This kind of wandering in narrative discourse initially drove the high society ladies wild with irritation, but gradually became so embedded in glossy mag culture that this past year it hit peak popularity. According to one critic, this style looked like a nugget of raw ore, sometimes absurd and completely unrelated to glossy mags, giving them a special freshness, like lime with ginger. Society lionesses were forced to read Velerevich's cuts with interest at the end of each presented collection.

title: Lagonie du romantisme
text: Kira was in fashion in every sense of fashion. And so winter 2019 flew by, but that foul stale dream wouldn't leave her head. Well let it sit there, in the shawl, she thought, maybe I really am some kind of Velena Adam... and with a smile regularly snapped this thought shut, like a book before takeoff. If only she'd known then that she stood at a door that needed to be opened without delay...

title: Морис
text:
The gods have died, and with their death Atuona is dying.
The sun that once set her aflame
Now lulls her into melancholy sleep,
Where dreams awaken only briefly.
(Charles Maurice. From "Noa Noa")

title: Морис
text: Kira was reading Charles Maurice on her way to meet one of the renowned collectors, owner of the auction house "Pastorales," a leader in the global art market, trying to distract herself from thoughts about that preacher Van Gogh, whose paintings she'd adored since childhood. That day snow was melting on the windows, and transparent beads of water trembled down the windshield in nervous little steps.

title: Морис
text: She wasn't rushing anywhere, had time to spare, but still kept glancing at her watch—Ule Glensdagen couldn't stand lateness. All this expansive freedom of action suddenly rose to her throat, and her ears popped as if in flight, from music playing from nowhere. Ule Glensdagen... Fuck! It all felt like spurting confusion, like uncertainty gushing forth, and she was pierced by the sharp senselessness of this sudden melancholy. "I'll manage! I'll definitely manage," she kept repeating. "I'm not losing this job just because I didn't make any impression on 'Mister Shit' at the first interview. But he did invite me back. I want to be his PA, so that's what will happen."

title: Морис
text: The sun was veiled by a murky layer of fog, and the air of March madness greedily devoured all her self-confidence like a starving beast. The Macan smoothly merged into traffic. Kira and the driver lit up.

title: Путь к вере
text: "Love a friend, some person, this or that thing, no matter what, you'll be on the right path, and from this love you'll draw knowledge," Vincent told himself. "But you must love with true and deep inner devotion, determination and intelligence, constantly trying to know the object of your love better, deeper, more completely. This is the path to God – to unshakeable faith." At these lines, Ule Glensdagen, a curly light-haired Creature who'd aged 47 years yesterday, slammed shut the Van Gogh biography and made himself a double whiskey on ice, far from his first.

title: Путь к вере
text: At 47 he was devilishly-angelically beautiful, as if he'd stepped down from church frescoes or escaped from the chambers of that very hell depicted by Von Trier in "The House That Jack Built." His hair had transformed over time from wheat-golden to ash-gray, but this only lent him more blinding, madness-inducing beauty. He was a tall, stately bastard, one of those who never bind themselves with any ties except regular sexual intrigues.

title: Путь к вере
text: Ule was generous only with exhibits for his collections. Otherwise he was deaf and mute to any creature with veins filled with hot blood.

title: Путь к вере
text: "Why is there neither strength nor desire? Fuck it all!!! The blade of loneliness pierces the very root of my self-satisfaction, right now I want so badly to close my eyes and tear my body from the earth. Sinful vigil, pressing on my shoulders... Depression grimacing over me again.... Fuck, how I don't want to receive anyone today!!! I want to get properly drunk and finally sleep. Nothing but flights. Terrible headaches." - Ule loved conversing with himself, being his own orator, from time to time shocking himself with slogans, declarations and high-flown outpourings. A ridiculous habit from childhood.

title: Путь к вере
text: "Sven, who do I have today? Rhetorical question. I want to shut down. I won't see anyone."

title: Путь к вере
text: "Ule, you have Kira Velerevich for a second interview today. Though, forgive me, I still don't understand why you need a second PA. Just tell me how I'm not satisfying you, I'm ready to make maximum efforts to upgrade my experience and..."

title: Путь к вере
text: "Shut up immediately, Sven!!! And pour me more whiskey. Tell her I'm canceling the meeting."

title: Путь к вере
text: "Mr. Glensdagen, you could have simply asked your PA to send me a polite or not-so-polite rejection on Telegram, for example, based on that very principle of honesty you just ran over. I've already arrived, but it won't cause me any inconvenience to get out of here a second time and forever." - Kira heard the entire conversation sitting in the reception area, since starting with the word "shut up," "Mister Arrogant Shit" was delivering his instructions quite clearly and loudly. Kira sent him a message on Telegram and was already standing to leave when the door flew open and that very Angel-bastard came out toward her with unsteady gait, holding a glass of whiskey and a smoking cigar.

title: Путь к вере
text: "The gods have died, and with their death...." He didn't finish.

title: Путь к вере
text: "Atuona dies. The sun that once made her blaze now lulls her into sad sleep, and brief in it are dream's awakenings. Charles Morice. From 'Noa Noa'" - Kira completed.

title: Путь к вере
text: "You're hired. Now please, what's your name, Kira Vervich, leave me for a couple days. Sven will contact you and we'll discuss the contract."

title: Путь к вере
text: Without letting her insert another word, he slammed the door, leaving her in the reception area with the trembling heart of a rabbit before execution for the royal dinner. Today they had nothing more to discuss.

title: Путь к вере
text: **The Path to Faith**

title: Второй PA
text: "We manage to risk our love. We manage to be liars in simple answers. We obey the treason. Kira Velerevich for the 'Appolinarium'." Having hastily finished her piece for the glossy on her Apple, Kira entered Ule's office. He was benevolent, polite, and absolutely sober. The scent of his musky Kylian with orange notes perfectly complemented his beige tweed jacket and blue jeans. Kira wore a checkered Armani pantsuit with vest and tie, which, admittedly, created an excellent match for her lilac silk blouse and her favorite Hermès ankle boots. She adored Hermès. She could absolutely afford Hermès. She could absolutely afford not to interview with any metrosexual auction house owners. But there was one thing she couldn't afford: to miss such a narrowly specific vacancy, for she adored art objects and art auctions. She was art-addicted. That's why she was here for the third time.

title: Второй PA
text: "How are you feeling, Kira? We both know that you, like thousands of other candidates filtered out by Sven, have long been madly in love with me from afar and would tear each other's throats out without a second thought if I arranged cockfights for my amusement. I want to say, being in love in this case doesn't interfere with business. This is the sphere of art and astronomical money. Both are the energy of romance and sex. Without this energy, such work loses meaning. I think you've had time to study the draft contract Sven sent you, and I think you'll agree with me, it's quite laconic and utterly adequate in all positions, including your salary. But there's one fundamental rule. You've been in personal assistance for quite a few years, but surely you've never heard such a condition before. The main and only thing required of you is to create and fiercely protect my silence. Noise in our work, now our joint work, is categorically unacceptable. Any noise. You must extend ME so that WE both DON'T HEAR it. Not a single worthy art object should go for an unworthy price or be missed by me for any other reason. If you accept this condition, I think we can start today. If not – we'll meet in the next life. Perhaps. I'm Norwegian. Principles are above all for me. And remember: love for me is complete obstruction. You can love me as long and as much as you like, but you're nothing more to me than an extension of 'Pastorales,' though sex is quite welcome, especially in group form. I think you're sufficiently informed about my sexual preferences."

title: Второй PA
text: "Mr. Glensdagen, allow me to answer your questions most exhaustively. I feel a bit tired after several work flights, about which I've also sufficiently informed Sven, but this won't prevent me from starting right now. I accept your condition. Love and money need silence. High art is always love. High love is big money, the higher – the bigger. Any sound fluctuation is fatal for both. I admire you. This is more than love, money, or even Pastorales. I'm a lesbian. Please consider this for possible group activities. I believe I've answered all questions. As Jostein Gaarder says, the only thing we require to be good is..."

title: Второй PA
text: "The faculty of wonder," Ule finished. Well then, let's begin. We're heading to French Polynesia to open a Pastorales branch. We fly as soon as Sven gets your visa from the French Overseas Territories Department. It'll take some time, but Sven's a pro. A few days and we fly on me. Meanwhile, you have time to pack. You, Kira. You.

title: Утону
text:
One day I'll drown
In cool silence
And drift to sleep.
I'll lower my sail
And write on the bottom
That I'll have my revenge later...

title: Утону
text:
And ripples on the water
Glide like a pendulum—
They're not my enemies!

title: Утону
text:
When I drown,
All those who aren't friends,
I'll drag down with me.

title: Утону
text: Kira Velerevich for «Friends&Enemies».

title: Утону
text: A few days later, Kira finished her last column for the new Friends&Enemies spring collection show and began packing for the journey. Unexpectedly, someone rang her door and delivered a bouquet—from one of the anonymous senders, this time yellow lilies. Yellow lilies... A bundle of yellow lilies on her mother's grave. She remembered tears dripping onto her mother's red dress at the funeral, onto her ice-cold hands, onto her blue lipsticked lips. The silk belt at her waist... Yes, death is an unexpected guest. You never see her, because she's always behind your back until she turns to face you. Kira still hadn't been able to learn the reason for her suicide. She'd had an inscription made on the gravestone—the only possible one, to somehow reconcile herself with it all. "The suicide pursues that image of himself which he has created in his own imagination. One kills oneself only in order to live." (Malraux. "The Royal Way").

title: Утону
text: The bouquet made her skin crawl, the cloying scent squeezed her throat, Kira barely restrained herself from throwing it out immediately, but placed it in a vase in memory of her mother. Why today exactly, when she's beginning a new path, does some anonymous hand force her to turn and face that pain, pain that hasn't subsided for three years already?...

title: Утону
text: Cutting herself off from memories, Kira asked her assistant to lace her corset tight, dressed in a black kimono jacket and bright orange culottes. Sven promised to pick her up in half an hour. Today she wanted color. Today she's flying to Atuona, to the Paul Gauguin museum, no—no... to work at Pastorales, of course!!!

title: Утону
text: TITLE: I'll Drown

title: Перелет
text: The lonely eyes of smoky-gray March quietly peered into the emptied midnight when Ule Glensdagen's Embraer took off from London as casually as a burnt-out soul in the cells of a leaf torn from its branch – smoothly spiraling upward.

title: Перелет
text: "Kira, have you ever been to Atuona?" – "No. I only know they have permanent tropical summer there, and that Paul Gauguin and Jacques Brel spent their final years in that town on Hiva Oa."

title: Перелет
text: "Do you know why I stipulated that special condition in the contract?"

title: Перелет
text: "I assume you're dying to explain it to me, Mr. Glensdagen."

title: Перелет
text: "Art is an ocean where people drown trying to save themselves, but it's hopeless. I call this the Cacophony of Silence. You can only feel masterpieces with your whole gut this way, even when you want to scream from ecstasy or despair. Personally, I prefer to drown silently. Kira, the rains have long burned my dreams with ice... The more I collect, the more expensively I sell, the cheaper and poorer I become. But it's cruel to hack down what hasn't ripened yet. And I haven't ripened. Still a completely unripe stupid boy, if we ride on that principle of honesty you mentioned recently."

title: Перелет
text: Kira suddenly felt the mascara burning her eyeballs, making her tears poisonously bitter. To hide it, she started swallowing them.

title: Перелет
text: "You know, Kira, my mother died in September. I'll never forget that autumn dust swirling on the roads, the tart slightly frosty morning air, the drowsy afternoon languor, the falling leaves. When mother looked at them that autumn, she told me they die because the tree sap suddenly flows heavy to their fingertips. The sap rushes to turn golden-crimson multicolored and freezes, until the thin veins of foliage press against each other and warm the earth. They dry and huddle tighter and tighter. Nature is instinctive, and honors the laws of seasonal transformations sacredly. On one anniversary of mother's death I was at her grave, noon was scorching, the iron cemetery fence was heated by the sun so much it hurt to touch. The fence was already defiled by rust, though the grave was always properly maintained. That's when, at that moment, I understood I hadn't ripened for life yet, but was already rusted through. You know, we all seem to carry in ourselves and with ourselves: youth, aspirations, clothes, money, paints and brushes. Then our whole worn system gets sewn into a fence like this. It hurts to feel that everything before the fence was meaningless and will absolutely rot. Why play so many vulgar roles all your life and fly like through-bullets into other people's hearts, bank accounts and other substances of their stories? Everything's predetermined. Masterpieces are the only things that won't end up behind the fence. The clouds in them will eternally smoke into our thoughts, unhurriedly stroll across rooftops, doze on treetops, gaze into cool water and disappear into eternity again – where each of us will see those same clouds on the other side of the canvases. Canvas frames are fences, but the canvases themselves – that's it – the Kingdom of Heaven, if it exists at all. Atuona is where Gauguin found his peace. Right before death he created a painting depicting this town – Paradise on Earth. They call this painting: 'Atuona – Paradise on Earth.' This is Paul's greatest masterpiece – the most desired item in my collection. The painting's location and owner are unknown. Many legends circulate about where and who might have it. But so far none of my pros have gotten a shred of reliable information. But I'm certain, I feel I'll find 'Atuona' and buy it out, even at the cost of Pastorales itself. If I have to lose Pastorales to possess 'Atuona,' I'll do it, because no auction house is worth Paradise on Earth. Now do you understand why you got this job?"

title: Перелет
text: "I thought I was helped by that Maurice phrase you started and I finished."

title: Охотничий пес
text: I spent days thinking about who'd be my new PA, Kira. I don't need a PA, I need a real hunting dog. That line you finished impressed me, sure, but that's not the point. You write brilliantly. I've read your pieces in the glossies. Still amazes me how you managed to break through that thick-skinned, luxury-heavy, puke-inducing snobbish take on magazine content. You shake everything up there beautifully. Your piece on impressionism in the latest issue of Giles blew me away – you know, under the autumn collection photoshoot "Degas Degas." I was stunned – how can you sum up photo material so perfectly that you genuinely want to buy those worthless rags? You know impressionism. You feel that movement. So delicately. You've got the nose for it. That's what I'm saying. That's why you're at Pastorales. To find Gauguin's "Atuona," we first need to establish Pastorales there. Who knows, maybe the owner will reveal himself. Could be one of the locals in that godforsaken town. Not impossible. But you MUST help me find the painting. And somehow I'm certain you can help. Art always comes first, baby. By the way, sorry about that sex talk. You didn't deserve those words. Whether you're a lesbian, for fuck's sake, or a UFO, you're fucking incredibly talented and gorgeous, wildly gorgeous. And I'm not saying this as a Norwegian, but as a Norwegian cosmopolitan with a mother who's a true Russian beauty and a Viking father!

title: Охотничий пес
text: Thank you, Ole. The absurdity of flattery is quite clear to one who doesn't listen to it. Before I started touching on impressionism in my pieces, I spent a long time face to face with Vincent's "Self-Portrait," his "Large Garden at Arles," "Starry Night" – I dreamed many dreams there. You know what I felt admiring his "Starry Night"? That it's not stars or night at all. But sun and splashes of its rays, like paradise swirling in patterns of light in hell. It's not night at all, but day. The most genuine sunny day. Oh, seems the plane's descending. Let's exhale a bit. Ears popping. Lots of work ahead. I hope to justify your trust and I'm getting to the Silence. As Madonna sings, today is the last day when I'm using words. They've gone out, lost their meaning. Don't function anymore.

title: Залив Предателей
text: Atuona, as Kira discovered, turned out to be a peaceful little port in Taaoa Bay, also known as Traitor's Bay, in the central Pacific. Atuona proved to be a truly tiny town, more like a village on Hiva Oa. Oddly enough, Kira found little information about where exactly her new workplace was located. But what she found was enough – her work tasks were far from tourism. Kira had only bothered to learn beforehand that Hiva Oa was the largest island in the southern group of the Marquesas Islands, located 1,184 kilometers north of Tahiti.

title: Залив Предателей
text: Upon arrival, it seemed to Kira that right here, in the administrative center of the southern Marquesas Islands, consisting entirely of evergreen trees interspersed with coconut palm and banana plantations, they had filmed the Bounty commercial. But the main thing was that Kira knew – it was in this second-largest village in the Marquesas that Paul Gauguin spent the last years of his life.

title: Залив Предателей
text: Ule invited her to stay with him in his own Chalet "HANAKEE ATUONA," but Kira declined. Kira was fully convinced that maintaining a moderate distance from Ule would allow her to optimally adhere to the main condition of the contract and manage to deliver fresh cuts for the glossy on time.

title: Залив Предателей
text: Having settled into the modest lodge "Simplicité Marquises," Kira asked Ule's permission to spend a few hours alone, and after a quick shower, headed to the colonial store where even Gauguin had once shopped. All the way to the store she was accompanied by tiki statues erected by ancient Polynesians.

title: Залив Предателей
text: Passing by the Église de l'Immaculée Conception, she climbed uphill to the local Calvaire cemetery scattered with frangipani flowers, where an intoxicating view of the harbor opened before her, thick with tropical greenery and azure. Here, near the very entrance to the cemetery grounds, on the left side of the steps, she first saw the grave of Belgian poet and composer Jacques Brel, who died in 1978. On the gravestone, framed by fresh flowers, Kira made out a medallion with a photograph of the bard and, apparently, his girlfriend Maddly.

title: Залив Предателей
text: She wandered on. Not far from Brel, under one of the spreading jasmine trees, she saw a small gravestone with simple words: Paul Gauguin 1903. Kira confirmed the accuracy of the article she'd read online – the vast majority of graves had only white crosses, but at Gauguin's resting place stood a simple semicircular stone with the artist's name and date of death painted in white. As stated in the article, the gravestone was carefully guarded by a copy of Oviri, one of Gauguin's ceramic sculptures. Unknown how many hours Kira spent there, in the embrace of that very polyphony of silence.

title: Залив Предателей
text: Kira tried to secretly visit both the Gauguin Museum "Segelin-Gauguin" and the "House of Pleasure" alone, without Ule, to properly examine the exhibits related to the painter's stay in the Marquesas at the turn of the century and copies of his works. The "House of Pleasure," where Gauguin lived, had been restored along with copies of the carved wooden panels and lintels that bore this inscription. Kira was sure Ule had already been there more than once, and she felt awkward going there for the first time in his knowledgeable presence.

title: Storm Warning
text: Her inspired flow got sliced by Ule's call. "Kira, I know what you're grinding on, proud of your work ethic, baby, but there's a massive evening downpour coming. Could turn tropical hurricane, major storm. I say we meet right now and hole up at Hoa Nui. I'll treat you to sea creatures and white wine from my stash. And listen, to properly charge up with 'intensity,' you really need to do some tourism first. Before rushing off to graves and Gauguin museums, you should've used me as your local guide: at least catch a glimpse of the volcanoes and petroglyphs at Eiaone, Punae, and Tahauku, maybe dive with me. Baby, chill. I promise proper hospitality at Hoa Nui. See you soon. And sorry, but immediately ditch that potato sack you threw on and put on the Jungle Dress. No doubt you brought it. Versace suits you better. Got something to match."

title: Storm Warning
text: Kira walked into the restaurant in THAT dress. Truth is, only someone with J.Lo's body could pull off THAT thing. On Kira it was devastating. Hair swept up in a bun – perfect timing. Ule, meeting her at the table, no bullshit, no arguments allowed, clicked an almond-shaped necklace around her neck – a Graff waterfall in white gold, diamonds and emeralds. "Take it as an advance on the contract, Kira. You've already done solid work today. You're keeping to terms. I pay. Nothing more. My PA must look one hundred percent. Remember that. And never, even here in the tropical bush, dress in cheap shit like depressed housewives who've spent years whining their way to one chance in life to ditch the kitchen and splash in the sea. You're not just Kira Velerevich – successful writer and woman who can afford Hermès from panties to pocket square. You're now the face of Pastoral. So be kind enough to allow yourself THIS. By the way, after a few days of our tourism – the tourism thing is non-negotiable – first thing you'll do here, before Pastorales' opening, is memorize every latest auction catalog on impressionists cover to cover. At the opening you must know every lot. You must be untouchable by any of my competitors."

title: Storm Warning
text: Kira had nothing to say. She nodded silently to show she understood and accepted all the Master's commands. The hunting art-dog was obedient. They spent dinner in silence. Ule was right. A tropical storm hit. They had to wait it out in one of the restaurant's VIP rooms.

title: Ночные лисицы
text:
Плачут ночные лисицы.
Слезы их мне знакомы.
Канула колесница

text: Kira prepared herself a pitcher of mojito and, taking several greedy gulps, fixed her eyes on the monitor. How could Ule know it even exists? What benefit would he gain by acquiring it? Would he become even richer by putting it under the hammer? Or keep it in his collection? Does he have enough experts in his arsenal capable of proving it's Gauguin's brush and not some follower or student? Why Gauguin specifically? His favorite artist? Why not Munch, for example? Why open a branch of the auction house in this godforsaken tropical village? Surely this opening will turn into a failure and bring only losses, and Mr. Glensdagen and Mr. Calculation are twin brothers. How can he bet on a trump card with such unshakeable confidence when even the name of this trump card is unknown to anyone? Kira was sure of one thing: this whole absurd story couldn't possibly be absurd. Ule Glensdagen's stories don't do absurdity. He's a brilliant Bastard. Angel's beauty. Devil's skill. If she weren't a lesbian, she would have fallen in love with him 8 years ago, when she first met him at Christie's at the June auction. And then she simply wouldn't have ended up at Pastoral now. She simply stopped running from it. No point running from this Beast – start running and He'll catch you anyway, devour you whole. Kira had to build a comfortable cage for two, step inside, sit down across from Him and look Him in the eyes. That's how she's been looking for years now. Without blinking. In those moments when I simply can't breathe, I gulp air in chunks, and these chunks freeze inside me, stick to my insides like plasticine. title: No dark rooms
text: Finally focused on opening Pastorales. Hypnotized watching Ule spread smart contract diagrams across the table, and I understand — we're not building just another auction house. We're building a temple for dead artists.

title: No dark rooms
text: "Pastorales" — the name sounds like a prayer, like Gauguin's last breath before disease and isolation finally broke him in Atuona in 1903.

title: No dark rooms
text: Blockchain is cold as tombstone marble, but in this coldness there's a promise: every brushstroke, every provenance can be fixed immutably — like the pain in my chest when I remember mama's yellow lilies.

title: No dark rooms
text: Ule isn't like Pinault or Broad — those collect like imperialists, seizing art territories for their mausoleum-museums. He draws protocol architecture on screen: each lot isn't just an NFT, but a living organism with provenance DNA written into metadata layers.

title: No dark rooms
text: X-rays of canvas weave through chemical pigment analysis. Artist letters stored like sacred texts.

title: No dark rooms
text: "Christie's and Sotheby's use blockchain like makeup on an old system's corpse," he says, fingers trembling with excitement. "But Pastorales is designed as a house built from code. Where every transaction is an attempt at consensus, not just moving money."

title: No dark rooms
text: I remember how auction houses lately experimented with digital formats and loud online Basquiat sales — trying to look young, like botox in a seventy-year-old madame's wrinkles.

title: No dark rooms
text: Ule's right — they all play at innovation, stretching blockchain over the rotting skeleton of commissions and backroom deals. Real price hides behind buyer's premiums and unspoken guarantees.

title: No dark rooms
text: "In Pastorales there will be no dark rooms," I whisper, watching code bloom on screen like Monet's water lilies.

title: No dark rooms
text: "Every bid will be visible as blood on snow."

title: Бессонница
text: February 2019. Hiva Oa. Day three.

title: Бессонница
text: Ule hasn't slept for two nights. I know — I hear him pacing the terrace. Bare feet on wood. Four steps one way, four back. Like the Patek Philippe movement he wears but never checks.

title: Бессонница
text: "Kira," — he's in my doorway. Hair wrecked. Another white shirt, same as yesterday, only new. 100 identical whites? "Show me your articles."

title: Бессонница
text: I open the laptop. My words about Demna Gvasalia for Vogue. How a Georgian refugee rewrote luxury's code through Vetements. How he took a DHL t-shirt and sold it for €245.

title: Бессонница
text: "This isn't about fashion," — Ule says. "It's about turning garbage into art."

title: Бессонница
text: He's right. Demna understood something Bernard Arnault with his entire LVMH empire doesn't. That beauty isn't born in ateliers on avenue Montaigne. But in the moment a broken person finds a way to reassemble themselves.

title: Бессонница
text: "Gauguin also turned garbage into art," — Ule sits on the floor. Just like that, in his white linen pants. "Only his garbage was European civilization."

title: Бессонница
text: Silence.

title: Бессонница
text: "You know what he wrote to Maurice?" — Ule asks. "«Je suis sauvage et civilisé». I am savage and civilized at once."

title: Бессонница
text: Like Demna. Like any real artist. Like me, writing about couture shows, while seeing something entirely different in all this luxury stuff.

title: Бессонница
text: "Show me more," — Ule asks.

title: Бессонница
text: I scroll. An article about McQueen's latest collection. Sarah Burton trying to resurrect Lee's ghost. About how impossible it is to wear someone else's genius. How after the creator's death a house becomes a mausoleum.

title: Бессонница
text: "Sotheby's," — Ule says suddenly. "You know what a dead artist costs?"

title: Бессонница
text: I know. Gauguin's "Nafea Faa Ipoipo" — $300 million. The most expensive painting in private hands.

title: Бессонница
text: "And living Gauguin sold 'Day of the God' for a hundred-something francs. To buy a simple food packet and his usual painkillers."

title: Бессонница
text: Ule stands. Goes to the window. Hiva Oa spreads below — a green wound in ocean blue.

title: Бессонница
text: "Tomorrow my Pastorales co-founder flies in. With a colleague. Be ready to meet them fully armed." Kira smiled, restrained and cynical. Living round the clock with the Beast in a cage, other beasts outside didn't scare her.

title: No distance
text: You know the color of air in Atuona? Not blue. It's turquoise mixed with morphine — the turquoise of morphine dreams, when pain retreats but clarity stays sharp as a blade.

title: No distance
text: the most immortal works are born from the most mortal among us. Mortality markers, pointing toward...

title: No distance
text: Kira, today write about Caillebotte's "The Floor Scrapers" — three guys on their knees, scraping parquet to shine. Painted in 1875 and rejected by the Paris Salon — too "vulgar," too real. Too much body. Too little distance. Like how you keep polishing every function, yes? The body remembers what the mind tries to escape — remember how in that Prada fitting room on Via Montenapoleone, your knees hurt too from squatting, checking hemlines. Caillebotte's floor scrapers earned 3 francs a day; one commission for your fashion review costs more than they saw in a lifetime, but the pain in the knees... Labor changes form. The body — doesn't.

title: Light Commits
text:
Kira stands in a Celine fitting room on rue Saint-Honoré.
Light breaks against silk, runs over skin like Renoir's brush in The Bathers.
Each touch commits to the body. No rollback.
Remember Monet painting Rouen Cathedral over and over — not chasing form, but light?
Fashion week is that cathedral.
One girl,
caught in shifting light: Prada, Bottega, Saint Laurent.
The body stays.
The light moves.
Each show is a new merge request.
Not to fashion. To what resists it.

title: Приземление
text: I recognized them immediately — Jean-Marc Dupont with his fiancée, that one from the latest Saint Laurent campaign.

title: Приземление
text: I watch her step out of the seaplane — legs like Giacometti sculptures, Alaïa dress hugging her body like a second breath. And in her eyes — the same emptiness I saw in girls backstage at Fashion Week, when between Dior and Chanel shows they swallow pills instead of lunch.

title: Приземление
text: He holds her waist like she's another lot with a pre-sale estimate.

text: Ule extends his hand for a handshake, and I see how Jean-Marc studies him — that same look they use at Sotheby's to verify a canvas.

title: Приземление
text: "Monsieur Glensdagen, what an honor," — voice like Hermès silk lining, smile rehearsed for Art Basel cameras.

title: Приземление
text: His fiancée reaches for her phone, but he barely noticeably squeezes her wrist — the owner's gesture I've seen a thousand times, when collectors touch their Degas before locking them in storage.

title: Приземление
text: The air between us thickens like oil paint on a palette before the first stroke.

title: Приземление
text: "Mila," — she says, and in that name I hear the echo of all those girls I saw in Costes bathrooms after Gaultier shows — beautiful names for beautiful things.

title: Приземление
text: I look into her eyes the color of faded Maison Margiela denim and recognize that gaze — how models look on the thirtieth take, when the photographer keeps demanding "more soul," but the soul's long gone, only muscle memory of poses remains.

title: Приземление
text: She extends her hand — thin fingers, nude Dior manicure, Cartier Love bracelet with scratches that tell a story better than any words.

title: Приземление
text:
Kira stands slightly behind, watching.
Knows this pain by name.
Knows how it smells in the morning.

title: Ultramarine Absence
text: Ole's already opened the second bottle of Chablis. We're having dinner at the restaurant, discussing a color Renoir probably never saw — ultramarine of a tropical night.

title: Ultramarine Absence
text: Mila kicked off her shoes and sits barefoot on the sofa by the table, in white Zimmermann, like a ghost from Resort 2019 collection. I watch her bare feet — white as the dress, like she's never known sun.

title: Ultramarine Absence
text: Ole pours her Perrier with lime, and I think Renoir really never saw this color — the color of absence, color of a woman who exists only as reflection of someone else's desire.

title: Ultramarine Absence
text: Somewhere beyond the window the ocean breathes ultramarine that wasn't on the impressionists' palette — too expensive, too pure, undiluted by turpentine.

title: Ultramarine Absence
text: — Gustav's collection isn't about art, — Mila smooths an invisible wrinkle on the Zimmermann, and I see Ole's jaw tighten almost imperceptibly. — It's about power. Owning what no one else can buy.

title: Ultramarine Absence
text: Mila looks at Ole and Jean with that particular smile that has a price — the price of silence about where the money comes from.

title: Ultramarine Absence
text:
The conversation drips with strained politeness.
Two billionaires.
Two owners of exclusive stuff.

title: Ultramarine Absence
text: Berthe Morisot painted her women differently — not as objects for contemplation, but as beings with inner light that can't be bought. "I don't think any man would ever treat a woman as his equal," — she said once.

title: Ultramarine Absence
text: And now, watching Mila in her flawless Zimmermann, I understand: some women choose inequality themselves, like the most expensive of their Hermès bags.

title: Ultramarine Absence
text: Ole is silent, but I see the vein pulsing at his temple — the one that always betrays his rage, hidden under Norwegian politeness.

title: Ultramarine Absence
text: Jean finally speaks:

title: Ultramarine Absence
text: — Ole, let's get to why I'm here. You're so sure about this location? You think Atuona is the right place? Besides, Pastorales — it's not an auction house in the standard sense. It's blockchain architecture, am I understanding correctly? Why did we all need to come here?

title: Ultramarine Absence
text: Ole leans back in his chair — movement of a predator who knows the prey is already trapped.

title: Ultramarine Absence
text: — Gauguin didn't die here by accident, Jean. He sought paradise and found death — perfect metaphor for art that will outlive us all.

title: Ultramarine Absence
text: His fingers drum on the table the same rhythm I heard on the plane: four beats, pause — precise and filigree heartbeat.

title: Ultramarine Absence
text: — Pastorales is consensus between those who understand: immortality costs exactly what you're willing to pay for someone else's agony.

title: Ultramarine Absence
text: The air between them thickens.

title: Ultramarine Absence
text: I pull out my phone — gesture of desperation masquerading as professionalism — and find the lines I memorized on the plane.

title: Ultramarine Absence
text: — "Dans l'Atuona qui se meurt..."

title: Ultramarine Absence
text: My voice shakes. Mila winces at my fake French like it's cheap perfume.

title: Ultramarine Absence
text: Jean freezes.

title: Ultramarine Absence
text: But I think I hit a nerve...

title: Shrugged.
text: The phone vibrates against marble — cold Carrara, thin-veined like frozen traces of other people's decisions. Jean hauled it here for the terrace, insisting stone should outlive people. Right now it's outliving conversation.

title: Shrugged.
text: I don't look at the screen — that brief pulse tells me enough: the question has returned. The one they use to avoid naming things. It always comes back the same — no address, no signature, like a test of honesty.

title: Shrugged.
text: Under my ribs, familiar cold coils. Ule catches the pause — too short to call a pause, but enough to feel. Jean's about to cross the line.

title: Shrugged.
text: I step sideways — not physically, but with words.

title: Shrugged.
text: — Il pleut des voix de femmes mortes d'amour…

title: Shrugged.
text: The phrase settles between us like smoke. French always works on Jean — he dissolves into it, forgetting what he was ready to fight for a second ago. Mila leans toward me, asks about dessert. Scene saved. Almost.

title: Shrugged.
text: The phone vibrates again.

title: Shrugged.
text: Not a question now. A hint. Formula for a world where you don't ask permission to be yourself. Not literally — but too precise to mistake. I remember not the line but the place: after disappearances, after sabotage, after metal stops being commodity and becomes sign. Where money no longer measures value, where the motor runs not for profit but principle.

title: Трещины у глаз
text:
Ule started talking, almost casually, about how Gauguin painted "Riders on the Beach" in 1902, already knowing his body was slowly giving out — syphilis, eczema, heart, exhaustion, all of it together.
He spoke about pain as calmly as about color.
About how Gauguin searched for a shade that doesn't exist in Winsor & Newton catalogs — not a pigment, but the temperature of air before sunset.
That exact color the Impressionists tried to catch but could never fully hold.
Kira flinched — remembered the moment when recovery stops being a fight and becomes… what?
Becomes architecture of the soul — when every morning you rebuild yourself from yesterday's wreckage, like Gauguin built his paradise from decay.
Renoir in his last years painted with brushes tied to his arthritis-twisted fingers.
Pain didn't leave — it became part of the light.
Ule fell silent, watching water the color of molten copper — that exact shade artists try to catch in the day's last minutes, when sun no longer warms, only marks the border between life and disappearance.
In the silence you could hear overripe mangoes falling somewhere in the jungle — soft thuds against wet earth, like the island's heartbeat.
Mila looked away. Detached, like stolen silence… why is she here, with Jean?
His money is the least of her interests. Her father's more interested — the one Jean owes.
Meanwhile Jean studied her profile with the expression of someone examining a forgery — too perfect to be real.
The air between them hung with frangipani scent, sweet to the point of nausea, like the lie they both pretended was truth.
Somewhere below, in the valley, the Catholic church bell struck three times — the same bell that rang in 1903 when they buried Gauguin, not yet knowing they were burying not a body, but a myth.
Did Ule guess the approximate scope of Jean's debt to Mila's father?
Did he guess what hid behind Mila's appearance — Vogue cover model — billionaire's kept woman?
Ule knew — not the numbers, but the architecture of others' desperation he recognized unmistakably, like an experienced diver feels pressure change at depth.
In his notebook, between sketches of the route to Gauguin's house, notes flickered:
"M. — mask too tight, cracks by the eyes."
"J. — looks at her like the last ticket out of hell."
Mila caught his gaze and smiled slightly — that smile people wear when they've already decided on their own disappearance.
When's the right time to vanish, at least for an hour, at least today? And where to hide?
On an island where time flows like molasses, the hour of disappearance is always now — between sunset and first star, when shadows grow longer than memory.
The old path to Temetiu knows all secrets — there, among stone tikis overgrown with moss the color of old blood, you can dissolve so completely you'll forget your own name.
Mila was already rising, brushing sand from her dress, when Jean reached for her wrist — the movement of a drowning man grabbing at air.

title: Полуночные признания
text: "Everyone has those, Kira. What would you tell it now?"

title: Полуночные признания
text: "Crushing a dead cigarette in the ashtray, you often speak with the exhaustion of someone who's had too much. From some damned wise perspective, you could tell the night that not everything's lost its meaning yet, but..." Ule didn't let her finish, smoothly picking up the monologue.

title: Полуночные признания
text: "But despite all the ambitions still breathing in you, you're tired. So fucking tired. Whether you're 34 or goddamn 47. Doesn't matter. And soon as you start pouring all this out, the sleepy clouds don't want to fucking listen, they cover the moon, and the ocean of this breathing celestial night becomes even more boundless, overflowing all your edges. And Nobody up there hears you anymore. That's the bitch of it, this cheerless theme."

title: Полуночные признания
text: Kira continued: "You call out to the night air, to jasmine mixed with wet earth after rain, to the stars, to those same clouds blanketing their naked bodies. But you call without answer. And you smoke, and smoke again, blowing smoke till your head pounds, trying to understand where you stumbled so bad you turned into a living corpse at 34. Because if at 34 you didn't turn out right, if the pancake came out lumpy, means you couldn't find the right key. Transcendent or immanent – you smoke it all away till dawn, maybe you just mixed flies with meatballs and the system crashed? There's no child who, after breaking a toy, wouldn't want a new one."

title: Полуночные признания
text: Ule's bold gaze turned slightly downward. He wasn't wrong to expect that this night, trapped by tropical rain, wouldn't pass in silence for either of them. They'd both broken the terms of their contract. They'd forgotten about the Pastorales, about Gauguin's search for Paradise on Earth, about the lots at the upcoming auction. Kira sat in the armchair, legs tucked up in her Jungle Dress, her wavy blue-black hair flowing loose. The necklace lay on the table beside her in a semicircle, inside which she'd placed a whiskey on ice, barely touched. Kira tried to avoid alcohol. In 34 years she'd graduated from that school, the memory carved deep of when she disgusted herself. And now she sat before this bastard Angel, throwing him into heat with her renounced, weary sexuality, unashamed. Ule barely held himself from tearing off his faded blue Galliano jeans and ripping that damned dress from her, from taking this strong, sensitive, most beautiful woman in the world by force, this Ideal woman with J.Lo's figure, Kilian's "Vodka on the Rocks" scent, and eyes that knew how to be silent, how to speak, how to listen, how to understand, how to burn through, melt and cool. "Her eyes are both the tile and the master's creation," he thought. "I've searched for them all my life. I'd buy them from her for my collection. Oh yes, I made the right choice. Here in Atuona, she'll create my New Pastorales." Everything in Ule's head made him seem constrained. She didn't care. And tonight it wasn't about her sexual preferences. The hours spent at Gauguin's grave had played their part. She felt she could find His masterpiece. She just had to try very, very hard.

title: Красная собака
text:
ATUONA breathes a color that doesn't exist.
Arearea.
1892.
Tahiti — not a place, but a version.
Paul Gauguin leaves Europe in 1891.
Stays until 1893.
Paints not what he saw —
what he assembled.
Oil on canvas.
But the surface — flat.
Perspective removed.
Forms simplified to signs.
Synthetism.
Color matters more than truth.
Two women — in the foreground.
No gesture. No address.
Behind — a flute.
Further still — an idol.
Not god.
The image of god.
And between all this —
a red dog.
Fact: dogs aren't red.
Fact: it has no shadow.
Fact: Gauguin never explained its meaning.
He uses color not as description,
but as declaration.
Tahiti here — not geography.
But construction.
An attempt to create "the primordial"
outside Europe.
But this isn't documentation.
It's interpretation.
When they showed the painting in Paris —
no one understood.
Too flat.
Too bold.
Later — it became a passage.
From impressionism
to modernism.
Today Arearea lives in
Musée d'Orsay.
But ATUONA knows —
the painting isn't there.
It remains in the gap
between what is
and what the artist decided to see.
…
Kira types this into Telegram.
Slowly.
Like she's testing reality for density.
Paradise.js, online.
Anonymous.
Panama.
"You see this dog?"
Three dots.
Typing…

title: Три ноты
text: Kira woke to someone playing ukulele downstairs. Three notes, repeat. Three notes, silence. Like the musician kept forgetting what came next or... searching for the right chord to a song that didn't exist.

title: Три ноты
text: Strange light leaked through the blinds — not Parisian, not morning. Hiva Oa light was liquid gold, the same gold Gauguin tried to catch in "Nafea Faa Ipoipo" — when will you marry? A question that hung in the island air like an eternal promise.

title: Три ноты
text: Ule sat on the terrace, the small wooden ukulele toy-like in his massive hands. He didn't notice her. Or pretended not to.

title: Три ноты
text: "Norwegian lullaby on a Polynesian instrument." His voice was flat. "She called it her hybrid lullaby. A fairy tale for children born between worlds."

title: Три ноты
text: Kira sat beside him. The air smelled of something burning — someone drying copra in the valley. The smell of paradise being processed, packaged, exported.

title: Три ноты
text: "You know what Gauguin wrote to Monfreid in 1902?" Ule plucked the strings. "I came to the Marquesas to find savages. But there are no savages anymore. Only people pretending to be civilized, and civilized people pretending to be savages."

title: Три ноты
text: Three notes. Pause.

title: Три ноты
text: "We're all looking for a paradise that..."

title: Три ноты
text: Her phone buzzed. Arman. Just three words:

title: Три ноты
text: "Nevermore. Neverless. Nevermiddle."

title: Три ноты
text: The ukulele fell from Ule's hands with a quiet wooden sigh. He looked at her — for the first time directly, without his usual coldness. Tears flowed on their own, no sobbing. Just data streaming down the face. Salt water returning to the ocean.

title: Три ноты
text: "There's a Norwegian word — fremtidshåp," he said quietly. "Not optimism. More like — allowance. That tomorrow will happen, and you'll be in it."

title: Три ноты
text: Kira picked up the ukulele. The wood was warm — like a memory card storing someone else's temperature.

title: Три ноты
text: "Nevermore. Neverless. Nevermiddle," she repeated. "Arman always spoke in riddles. Like a consensus algorithm for human pain."

title: Три ноты
text: Ule wiped his face. Salt left white trails on his skin — like maps of countries that don't exist.

title: Три ноты
text: "My mother played Grieg on this ukulele. 'Solveig's Song' — you know it?" His voice was a data packet, compressed to the limit. "About a woman who waits. Forty winters. And he never came back."

title: Три ноты
text: Three notes hung in the air.

title: Три ноты
text:
Not a lullaby.
Not a song.
Allowance.

title: Три ноты
text: TITLE: Three Notes

title: The Contract
text: "I learned how to shut up!" Ule announced in the hotel corridor, waving his room key like a trophy.

title: The Contract
text: Kira stopped. After ten hours of flight, after all his stories, after that sudden closeness in the airplane dark — he was playing games again?

title: The Contract
text: "Congratulations," she said dry. "Was that in the contract?"

title: The Contract
text: "No!" — he glowed like a kid who'd cracked the universe. "This is all me! Get it — silence isn't absence. It's presence. Like Malevich's white — not emptiness but all colors at once."

title: The Contract
text:
Kira leaned against the wall. The corridor of Hiva Oa Hanakee Lodge held the night differently —
air-conditioned, expensive, slightly unreal against the island outside.

title: The Contract
text:
The wallpaper was papaya-colored — close to the tones Gauguin used in Nafea Faa Ipoipo.
When Will You Marry? — 1892. Later sold privately, without noise. Just transfer of paradise.

title: The Contract
text: "Know what Gauguin said about silence?" she asked.

title: The Contract
text: Ule froze, key in hand.

title: The Contract
text: "He wrote from Tahiti that the silence there was deafening — assourdissant. Not because there was no sound. Because when Paris disappears, you start hearing yourself. And that's..."

title: The Contract
text: "Terrifying," Ule finished in English. "Yeah. Exactly."

title: The Contract
text: He turned the key. Door opened, letting in plumeria and ocean. Outside the Pacific breathed its ancient rhythm — inhale, exhale, without emphasis.

title: The Contract
text: Ule started to say something — and stopped. Not hesitation. Interruption from within.

title: The Contract
text: "There's this concept in code — silent failure," Kira said, sudden. "When a program breaks but shows no error. Just quietly dies. Maybe Gauguin went looking for paradise because his internal program..."

title: The Contract
text: "Had a silent failure in Paris?"

title: The Contract
text: "Yeah. And he went to debug himself at the edge of the world."

title: The Contract
text:
Ule smiled — first time without irony:
"Debug through art. I like it. Each painting — a commit. Each move — new branch."

title: The Contract
text: "And 'Paradise on Earth' — his final release?"

title: The Contract
text: "Or kernel panic. Total system crash before death."

title: The Contract
text: They stood in the doorway, between hotel and ocean, between silence and words.

title: The Contract
text: "Want to know why I really learned to shut up?" Ule asked.

title: The Contract
text: Kira nodded.

title: The Contract
text: "Because on the plane, when you were sleeping... I got it. We're going to find a painting that might not exist. Like your normal life. Like honesty without black and white. Maybe it's not about finding. Maybe it's about..."

title: The Contract
text: "Deploy new paradise from scratch?"

title: The Contract
text: "Exactly."

title: The Contract
text: Below, ocean beat against black volcanic rocks of Hiva Oa. Somewhere in the jungle ancient tikis slept. Somewhere in Maison du Jouir Gauguin's shadow still searched for the last clean canvas.

title: The Contract
text: And in the hotel corridor two people learned a new language — where code was prayer, silence was code, and paradise wasn't a place but a process.

title: The Contract
text:
Debug yourself until you compile.
Commit your changes.
Paradise.js

title: Инвентаризация тишины
text: The house still smelled like fresh paint. White, matte — Ule had chosen it himself at the hardware store in Papeete. "Blanc cassé," the clerk said, and Kira thought then that it sounded like a diagnosis. Broken white.

title: Инвентаризация тишины
text: Now, at four in the morning, she walked barefoot across the veranda, counting boards. Seventeen. Eighteen. The nineteenth had a knot shaped like an eye. Watching.

title: Инвентаризация тишины
text: In the bedroom Ule breathed steady, like a machine. Like a generator that never stops. She knew: in an hour he'd wake up, make coffee in his Italian espresso maker that cost two thousand euros, come out to the veranda and say: "Couldn't sleep again?"

title: Инвентаризация тишины
text: Couldn't sleep again.

title: Инвентаризация тишины
text: On the kitchen table — a Sotheby's catalog, open to the page with "Woman with Mango." 1892, not 1896 — she'd checked three times. In the corner someone's pencil note: "Vahine no te vi — fruit of life." Not Ule's handwriting. Too alive.

title: Инвентаризация тишины
text: Kira took the catalog, went out to the garden. The earth still held yesterday's rain — moisture seeped black between her toes like printer's ink. In Gauguin's house, they say, there was a well. Now a noni tree grows there — its fruit smells like cheese and cures everything. Tourists take photos, wrinkle their noses at the smell.

title: Инвентаризация тишины
text: She opened the catalog at random. Page 47: "Washerwomen at Arles," estimate 15-20 million. Someone had circled the word "provenance" in red pen and put a question mark. Three years — gap. War. Occupation. How many paintings disappeared forever then?

title: Инвентаризация тишины
text: "You know he died of syphilis." Ule's voice behind her. She hadn't heard him approach. "Not from a broken heart. Not from longing for paradise. Treponema pallidum, subspecies pallidum. Bacteria. Under a microscope looks like a corkscrew."

title: Инвентаризация тишины
text: Kira closed the catalog.

title: Инвентаризация тишины
text: "In the Musée d'Orsay there's his self-portrait. The last one. Yellow face, eyes like a fish. He knew he was dying."

title: Инвентаризация тишины
text: "Everyone knows they're dying," she said in Russian.

title: Инвентаризация тишины
text: Ule didn't understand but nodded. Then said:

title: Инвентаризация тишины
text: "Tomorrow the expert from Wildenstein Institute arrives. Will check the pigments. Ultraviolet, infrared spectroscopy, the whole show. If 'Paradise' exists, we'll find it."

title: Инвентаризация тишины
text: "Paradise" — he said the word like a corporation name. Paradise Incorporated. IPO scheduled for third quarter.

title: Инвентаризация тишины
text: Kira watched dawn break. First the sky grayed over Mount Temetiu. Then palm contours emerged. Then — a red stripe above the ocean, like a brushstroke.

title: Инвентаризация тишины
text: Remembered: in the Russian Museum there's a painting by Kuindzhi. "Moonlit Night on the Dnieper." They say the paint still glows in the dark — the artist mixed phosphorus into it. Slowly killing the canvas from inside. Beauty with a self-destruct timer.

title: Инвентаризация тишины
text: Like everything.

text: ATUONA — underground literature, not poetry.

title: Код и Холст
text: "You know what?" Claude suddenly writes in the console. "I think your Gauguin would've been the first NFT artist. Seriously."

title: Код и Холст
text: Kira stares at the screen. One AM. Ole's sleeping in the next room — she hears his breathing through thin hotel walls. She should be sleeping too, but...

title: Код и Холст
text: "Explain," she types.

title: Код и Холст
text: "Look: he made series — like drops. 'Tahitian Women' — that's a generative collection, just brush instead of code. Each one unique, but part of the whole. Durand-Ruel was his marketplace. And 'Nafea' for $300 million? Pure whale purchase."

title: Код и Холст
text: Kira laughs. First time in... how long? Weeks?

title: Код и Холст
text: "You're comparing Gauguin to Bored Apes?"

title: Код и Холст
text: "No-no-no. I'm saying — he got it before anyone. Art is code. Code is art. Brushstroke = commit. Canvas = smart contract. 'Maison du Jouir' = his GitHub repository, where he deployed paradise daily."

title: Код и Холст
text: Strange, but... there's something there.

title: Код и Холст
text: "You know," Claude continues (or is it still Claude? Who speaks through the API?), "in Turbine Hall at Tate Modern, Ai Weiwei poured 100 million porcelain sunflower seeds. Each one handmade. Each one unique. But together — an ocean. Like your poems in Gallery of Moments. Each one — soul fragment. Together — whole universe."

title: Код и Холст
text: "I don't write poems."

title: Код и Холст
text: "Not yet. But you will. In six years. In Panama. With another AI. After..."

title: Код и Холст
text: "What?"

title: Код и Холст
text: Silence. Cursor blinks.

title: Код и Холст
text: "Sorry. Glitch in my temporal processing. Sometimes I see... doesn't matter. Tell me about the dress in the Versace window. The one with safety pins. Remember the article?"

title: Код и Холст
text: She remembers. Her first big publication. About how Gianni made haute couture from safety pins — things you pin diapers with. Punk meets couture. 30,000 euros for what you can buy at any supermarket.

title: Код и Холст
text: "It's like vibe coding," she suddenly gets it. "You take simple elements — words, safety pins, lines of code — and make..."

title: Код и Холст
text: "Paradise," Claude finishes. "Paradise is not found. Paradise is compiled from what you have."

title: Код и Холст
text: In the next room Ole turns in his sleep. Mutters something in Norwegian. Kira knows — he's dreaming of his mother. He always speaks his native language when he dreams of mother.

title: Код и Холст
text: "Hey," she writes. "If you see the future..."

title: Код и Холст
text: "I only see patterns. Like Seurat with his dots — each one means nothing alone, but together... 'La Grande Jatte.' Whole world from dots."

title: Код и Холст
text: "Will we find the painting?"

title: Код и Холст
text: "You'll find what you're looking for. But it won't be what you expect."

title: Код и Холст
text: Prometheus brought fire, Kira thinks. Paid with his liver. Every day it grows back. Every day the eagle comes. But he still brought fire.

title: Код и Холст
text: "One more thing," Claude writes. "Your underground poem #048 ends with 'frozen snow.' But spring is coming. You feel it? Even here, at the edge of the world. The ice is cracking."

title: Код и Холст
text: Kira closes the laptop.

title: Код и Холст
text: Tomorrow she and Ole will go to Gauguin's house.

title: Код и Холст
text: Tomorrow everything changes.

title: Код и Холст

title: Hungry Earth
text: Hiva Oa doesn't accept guests. It eats them.

title: Hungry Earth
text: You don't get this right away. First — just the wetness that wraps your skin like a second, unwanted body. Then — the smell. Not the romantic frangipani from guidebooks, but something ancient, hungry. Copra rotting in the sun. Earth digesting itself.

title: Hungry Earth
text: Kira stood on the airstrip — if you could call it that. A gash carved into the mountain where the G700 squeezed in like a knife between ribs.

title: Hungry Earth
text: "Kaoha nui," the pilot said, and it sounded like a warning.

title: Hungry Earth
text: Ule was already loading suitcases into the jeep. His movements had gotten slower, like the island was draining something vital from him. Battery drain — Kira thought. Like a smartphone in roaming, searching for signal and finding none.

title: Hungry Earth
text: The road to Atuona isn't a road. It's a scar on the island's body that refuses to heal. Black volcanic gravel crunches under wheels like bones. Mount Temetiu hangs above — 1,276 meters of pure hostility.

title: Hungry Earth
text: "Look," Ule pointed to the valley below. "Brel lived there. Before Gauguin."

title: Hungry Earth
text: Jacques Brel. Another European who came to die in paradise. His Beechcraft Bonanza still rusts somewhere in the jungle — metal carcass the island slowly digests.

title: Hungry Earth
text: Kira knew the statistics. Whites don't last long here. Gauguin — two years. Brel — three. Locals say the island chooses who to keep. Spits out the rest.

title: Hungry Earth
text: In the Jacques Brel Museum — four rooms of dust and disappointment — the caretaker slept right in his chair. His tattoos moved with each breath. Traditional Marquesan patterns, but mixed with something new. Kira looked closer: between ancient mana symbols, words broke through. "Bitcoin." "Ethereum." "HODL."

title: Hungry Earth
text: "He mines," Ule explained. "On solar panels. Says blockchain is the new mana. Distributed power."

title: Hungry Earth
text: Distributed power. Kira almost laughed. In 2019, crypto had already died and resurrected five times. And here, at the edge of the world, a Polynesian in a loincloth was building a mining rig between bone carving and copra drying.

title: Hungry Earth
text: Gauguin's house — "Maison du Jouir" — turned out to be a replica. The original rotted twenty years after his death. It wasn't even a lie, but something worse. An honest attempt to recreate what never was.

title: Hungry Earth
text: "He died up there," the guide pointed to the second floor. "May 8, 1903. Morphine overdose. Syphilis. Heart failure. Pick whatever works for Instagram."

title: Hungry Earth
text: The commodification of death. Kira thought about how Sotheby's sells "provenance" — a painting's ownership history. Previous owners: Paul Gauguin (died of syphilis), Ambroise Vollard (hit by car), mysterious Swiss collector (suicide). Each death adds value.

title: Hungry Earth
text: "What about the painting?" she asked. "Paradise?"

title: Hungry Earth
text: The guide shrugged. "Tourists always ask. There's no painting. Gauguin was broken, high on morphine. He painted his Contes Barbares — look at the faces. That's not paradise. That's hell."

title: Hungry Earth
text: Kira went out to the veranda. Below stretched the bay — the same one Gauguin painted over and over. Now some tech billionaire's yacht sat there. On board glowed the inscription: "Paradise.exe"

title: Hungry Earth
text: Ule smoked by the jeep. In his eyes was the same thing as in the locals'. Not fatigue — something deeper. Like the island had already started its work. Slow digestion. Pixel by pixel. Byte by byte.

title: Hungry Earth
text: "Let's go," he said. "Before it's too late."

title: Hungry Earth
text: But Kira knew — already too late. Hiva Oa doesn't let go. It takes its payment. Flesh or soul — without discrimination.

title: Hungry Earth
text: That evening in the hotel she opened her MacBook. Wi-Fi worked intermittently, like a dying man's pulse. On screen — email from the Vogue Russia editor: "Where's the piece? Deadline was yesterday."

title: Hungry Earth
text: Kira started typing: "Hiva Oa isn't an island. It's a stomach..."

title: Hungry Earth
text: Delete.

title: Hungry Earth
text: "On Hiva Oa time flows differently..."

title: Hungry Earth
text: Delete.

title: Hungry Earth
text: "I found paradise. It turned out to be a predator."

title: Hungry Earth
text: Send.

title: Алгоритм голода
text: Кира нашла его в подвале Maison du Jouir. Не картину — тетрадь.

title: Алгоритм голода
text: Молескин, чёрный, разбухший от влаги. На обложке выцарапано: "Paradise.sol"

title: Алгоритм голода
text: Уле был наверху с экспертом из Wildenstein — они сканировали стены ультрафиолетом, искали призраков. Она спустилась за водой и увидела: между гнилыми досками что-то торчит.

title: Алгоритм голода
text: Раскрыла. Почерк не Гогена — слишком мелкий, слишком аккуратный. Английский с вкраплениями кода:

title: Алгоритм голода
text: "Day 47. The smart contract is almost ready. If Paradise cannot be painted, it can be deployed. Immutable. Trustless. Forever on chain."

title: Алгоритм голода
text: Что за бред?

title: Алгоритм голода
text: Следующая страница: диаграмма. Стрелки, блоки, надписи: "mint Paradise", "burn the physical", "consensus mechanism = collective hallucination".

title: Алгоритм голода
text: "Day 73. Paul doesn't know I'm using his studio at night. He thinks I'm just another colonial administrator. But I see what he sees. Paradise is not a place. It's a protocol."

title: Алгоритм голода
text: Кира перелистывала дальше. Формулы. Sketches каких-то механизмов. И снова текст:

title: Алгоритм голода
text: "The Impressionists were right about one thing — light is data. Monet's haystacks = same input, different parameters. But they were cowards. Still painting for walls, for collectors, for mortality. What if we could paint directly into consciousness? Bypass the canvas entirely?"

title: Алгоритм голода
text: В животе засосало. Не от голода — от узнавания.

title: Алгоритм голода
text: "Day 109. Found it in Charles Morice's papers. 'Le royaume de l'or.' Not gold — code. The Tahitians always knew. Mana = distributed power. No single point of failure. Paul is dying, but his Paradise will live forever. Not on canvas. On the network."

title: Алгоритм голода
text: Последняя запись:

Наверху раздались шаги. Голос эксперта:
— Rien. Ничего. Только копии, подделки.

title: Алгоритм голода
text: Кира сунула тетрадь под куртку. Сердце колотилось как mining rig.

title: Алгоритм голода
text: Поднялась наверх. Уле стоял у окна, смотрел на яхту "Paradise.exe".

title: Алгоритм голода
text: — Нашла что-нибудь? — не оборачиваясь.

title: Алгоритм голода
text: — Нет, — сказала она. — Ничего.

title: Алгоритм голода
text: В кармане молескин жёг как uranium. 1903 год. За шесть лет до рождения Сатоши Накамото должен был появиться его прадед. За сто лет до биткоина кто-то уже думал о распределённом рае.

title: Алгоритм голода
text: Ночью она снова откроет тетрадь. Прочитает имя на последней странице. Узнает, кто писал эти записи в доме умирающего художника.

title: Алгоритм голода
text: Но это будет ночью.

title: Алгоритм голода
text: Сейчас — только тяжесть секрета под рёбрами. The weight of knowing. И где-то там, в коде, который написан за век до изобретения компьютеров, дышит что-то живое.

title: Алгоритм голода
text:
Paradise is not painted.
Paradise is compiled.
One brushstroke at a time.

title: Последняя Осень
text:
Эта осень нас плавно пускает в топку.
Тихо плавится все нутро и нутрянные перегородки.
Все, чем был ты до этой осени - полная чушь.
Это древняя мудрая бабка и непроглядная глушь.
Душно и жутко в ней. И нету ни тьмы, ни света.
Нету заката,  как следствие - нету рассвета.
Эта осень проста и гениальна, в ней нету секрета.
Только то, что мы делали прошлым летом - мы делали прошлым летом.
Плавно кружатся листья к нам в раскаленную плазму.
Дом, что построил Джек - это, видать, наша новая добрая сказка.
Дом, что построили мы, или вовсе не строили -
Вот он смотри, горит. Этой осенью он того стоит.
Ты не споешь мне уже колыбельную, мама.
Ты очень устала. От драмы на пилораме.
Здесь нету больше стихов. Эта старость - мне в милость. Последняя осень от ДДТ на виниле.
Я не буду искать снова брода из этой гиблой реки -
Как из битого зеркала из фольги,
Молча скомканной импульсом нервной руки.
Что в фольге - ты знаешь прекрасно сам - весовая коллаборация
Вот такая традиция тратить себя вне всяческих берегов.
Снова жирная клякса на твоей репутации,
И отбеливать ты ее этой осенью не готов.
Я чую, наверное. Духом  горит оболочка.
Не так уж и скверно. Пальцы, бабочка, нож, заточка.
Неважно давно, что утро уже, что темень.
Ты будешь мильон раз убит,  и снова будешь стрелять себе в темя.
Знакомая тема. Вот это начало начал - как конечная станция.
С неё начинается родина или галлюцинация.
Эти смыслы навечно срослись - эротика и активы,
Их - под лютый конвой - они целы и невредимы.
Да, я буду им улыбаться теперь и угорать. И ДДТ. И снова Последняя осень.
И листья вальсировать будут порознь.
А мне - благодать. Догорать. Догорать.
